text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY

- Alfred Kokh's resignation as head of the State Property Committee in the wake of the Svyazinvest share auction scandal proves that Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais does not want to be seen as too close to any of Russia's powerful banking groups.
- Russian cosmonauts return to Earth after a 185-day mission plagued by mishaps and glitches.

- Plans for a meeting between President Boris Yeltsin and Chechen separatist leader Aslan Maskhadov were thrown into confusion by unconfirmed reports that a Russian military plane flew over regional capital Grozny on Wednesday.
- Russians will be able to legally buy cut diamonds starting this autumn.
- Rebel Tajik commander Makhmud Khudoyberdyev has laid down his arms in exchange for a promise he will not be persecuted by the authorities in Dushanbe.
- The Russian and British special services have conducted a joint operation to stop a 200-kilo shipment of cocaine from South America to Russia.

- Shares in Russian gas monopoly Gazprom shot up at yesterday's session, prompting rumours speculators managed to find a loophole in the legislation allowing them to buy shares in Moscow and sell them in London at more than twice the price.
- Dmitry Vasilyev, head of the Federal Securities Commission, has launched a public attack against the appointment of a U.S. expert to head an important securities market advisory body.
- Negotiations between Russia, Ukraine and Kazakhstan to set up a joint venture to produce nuclear fuel for Ukrainian power stations have fallen through.
SEVODNYA
- The Moscow government is setting up a special commission which will control all food products imported into the city.

- Head of the State Property Committee Alfred Kokh, having beefed up the state budget at the expense of his own image, is handing over his post to Maxim Boiko, another major player in the team of Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais.

- The government should go out of its way to return the Purneftegaz oil company to the giant Rosneft oil producer if it wants Rosneft to fetch a decent sum of money for the budget when it is finally privatised.
- Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov has asked Russian peacekeepers in the troubled republic to disarm the troops of the defeated rebel commander Makhmud Khudoyberdyev.
- President Yeltsin says he is satisfied the government is paying back its debts to public sector workers on schedule.
- Russian energy monopoly UES would like to see major changes to the draft tax code before it is adopted by the Duma.
- The fate of the new tax code seems more and more unclear as different forces opposed to its adoption form a united front.
- Egypt has joined in the anti-dumping campaign against Russian steel producers.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- Europe recommends that Tallinn make Russian the second official language in the republic.
- Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin has managed to get the head of the State Property Committee Alfred Kokh relieved of his post.
- Russian security services have worked out a doctrine of Russia's information security.
IZVESTIA
- The World Bank will provide guarantees against sovereign risks in Russia for the huge Sea Launch international project to launch space craft from an oil rig stationed on the Equator.
- Mutinous Tajik military commander Makhmud Khudoyberdyev has laid down his arms after a week of clashes with government troops.
- The security services of Russia and Britain confiscated a huge shipment of cocaine from South America to Siberia.
- Russia should do its utmost to prevent a partition of Tajikistan, says Deputy Foreign Minister Boris Pastukhov.
- U.S. gold-mining companies are likely to follow in the steps of international oil giants already lining up to explore Azerbaijan's natural resources.
ROSSIISKIYE VESTI
- The harvesting campaign in southern Russia is running behind schedule for lack of money and equipment.
- Opinion polls show that about 40 percent of Russians think rouble redenomination will have a negative impact.
- The opposition in the Duma is limbering up for a new bout of confrontation with the government this autumn.
- A slow-burning conflict between shareholders of the giant Magnitogorsk Metallurgical Plant is threatening to break out into an international scandal.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS

- President Boris Yeltsin, on a visit to the Khrunichev space design centre, put the blame for the recent mishaps in space on Russian cosmonauts in an apparent attempt to turn the spotlight away from technical problems dogging Russia's run-down Mir space station.

- Russian special services in Tajikistan were too slow to react to the latest round of fighting in Dushanbe and almost allowed a rebel commander to perpetrate a coup d'etat, says an unidentified source in the Tajik government in an interview.
--Andrei Shukshin, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
